svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.27.5.1 Attachment
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.27 CLADDING
Attachment

g.text: Sheathing that may hold the cladding, (2), (3)
Sentence (2): vertical lumber, stucco lath or reinforcing,
vertically applied vinyl siding, vertically applied insulated vinyl
Sentence (3): vertically applied metal siding, and wood shingles

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Except as permitted by Sentences (2) to (5), cladding is
fastened to the framing members or furring members, or
to blocking between the framing members.
Vertical lumber, stucco lath or reinforcing, vertically
applied vinyl siding, vertically applied insulated vinyl
siding, and polypropylene siding are permitted to be
attached to sheathing only where the sheathing consists
of not less than
(a) 14.3 mm (9/16″) lumber, (b) 12.5 mm (½″) plywood or
waferboard, or (c) 11 mm (7/16″) OSB.
Vertically applied metal siding and wood shingles and
shakes are permitted to be attached to the sheathing
only where the sheathing consists of not less than
(a) 14.3 mm (9/16″) lumber, (b) 7.5 mm (5/16″) plywood, or
(c) 7.5 mm (5/16″) OSB or waferboard.
Where wood shingles or shakes are applied to sheathing
which is not suitable for attaching the shingles or
shakes, the shingles or shakes are permitted to be
attached to a wood lath not less than 38 mm by 9.5 mm
(1½″ by ⅜″) thick securely nailed to the framing and
applied as described in Article 9.27.7.5.
Cladding, trim and furring members are permitted to be
attached to the web fastening strips of flat wall
insulating concrete form units using screws in
accordance with Sentence 9.27.5.4.(2).
Drawn: one example each for Sentences (1), (4) and (5). Lath, shingle and strip spacing are illustration only.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.27.5.1. (page 9-259)
